cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. No cheers. The text says they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit (Luke 24:37). Jesus says, "Peace be with you." (Luke 24:36), and they're still startled and frightened. I think a few of them stopped breathing for a second.

The answer is spirit, friends. The text says they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit. Jesus answers that guess right away in the next verses. He's got hands, feet, flesh and bones to show them.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, "Touch Me and see…" (Luke 24:39). He doesn't just talk His way out of the confusion. He invites them to check for themselves. A man who tells you to touch Him has nothing to hide.

The reason is that a spirit has no flesh and bones, friends. Jesus says, "…for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have." (Luke 24:39). He points to what they can see right in front of them. And He tells them to touch Him and see.

He asks for something to eat, friends. He asks, "Do you have anything here to eat?" (Luke 24:41). Out of everything He could say in that moment, He asks about food. I respect a man who gets to the point, because that's how I feel around a fresh batch.

The answer is a piece of broiled fish, friends. They gave Him a piece of broiled fish, and He took it and ate it in front of them (Luke 24:42-43). They were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement when He asked for something to eat (Luke 24:41). Fish on the menu, and all of them watching.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, "Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms." (Luke 24:44). Not a piece of it and not half. He says everything, and that's a lot of Scripture pointing one way.

He opens their minds, friends. The text says, "Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures." (Luke 24:45). Understanding doesn't come from the disciples alone here. Jesus opens their minds Himself.

What gets proclaimed is repentance and forgiveness of sins, friends. Jesus says, "…in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem." (Luke 24:47). It's going out in His name, and it's going out to all nations. That's a lot of doors to knock on.

The answer is Jerusalem, friends. Jesus says it will be proclaimed to all nations, "…beginning in Jerusalem." (Luke 24:47). Earlier in this chapter, the disciples had gathered together in Jerusalem (Luke 24:33). The starting line is the city they're already in.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus tells them, "You are witnesses of these things." (Luke 24:48). Right before that, He tells them what is written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day (Luke 24:46). I think that's a weighty job, and He puts it right on them.

They stay until they're clothed with power from on high, friends. Jesus says, "But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high." (Luke 24:49). They're not told to start on their own strength. They're told to wait for the promise He's sending, and the waiting has a clear end.

He is carried up into heaven, friends. The text says, "While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven." (Luke 24:51). It happens right in the middle of the blessing. The last thing the disciples get from Him in this passage is a blessing.

The answer is temple, friends. The text says they were "…praising God continually in the temple." (Luke 24:53). That's where this passage ends, with them back in Jerusalem and full of praise. It's a joyful place to land.
